axes.model_access: Multi-model aggregation + in-house hybrid: the official site lists 64+ models (Veo/Ideogram/Runway/Luma/Flux/Gemini etc.); the in-house Krea 2 line; a real-time generation line. The model list changes with plans and launches, so the signed-in catalogue is authoritative.
axes.runtime: Web (krea.ai); generation runs in Krea's cloud and the real-time canvas is operated in the browser. There is no official offline client or local weight download; low latency is the selling point, and no concrete SLA or concurrency figure is listed publicly.
axes.local_files: Works and projects are stored account-side in the cloud, with downloads landing locally. Whether LoRA training artefacts can be exported locally is not itemised on public pages; the product surface has no local inference or offline generation entry.
axes.background: Real-time generation is the selling point (output as you type/draw); batch or long jobs queue in the cloud, and the product surface has no pause, resume or task-position control. Shutting the client down does not change the cloud job.
axes.tools: Real-time canvas, LoRA fine-tuning, an upscaling line, video-model aggregation (Veo/Runway etc.); an API surface exists but public documentation is limited, and MCP is not part of the listed capability surface.
axes.context: Organised by projects/boards; the product surface has no cross-session memory entry. The real-time canvas's "current frame" is in-session state, not persistent memory.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system; the Terms of Use (2024-05-20 version) grant Krea a broad licence over User Submissions, and commercial rights vary by tier. Marketing says "Do not train"; the binding constraint is the privacy-page text.
axes.fit: Fits: real-time interactive creation, switching between multiple vendors' models on one platform, cloud LoRA training. Does not fit: wanting open weights or offline use, deep per-model parameter control, or treating aggregation as "best at everything".

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **The real quality-latency curves of the real-time line vs. the frontier line** (same-prompt comparison)
- **Whether aggregated models' outputs are post-processed by Krea** (upscaling/filter chains)
- **The export and reuse surface of LoRA training artifacts**
unknowns:
- Upscaling ceiling (official copy mentions 22K, the fetched snapshot did not show it — not verified item by item)
- The training-terms original text and its clause-level correspondence to "Do not train" (not verified line by line)
- The API's model coverage and quotas (not verified item by item)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
related: It is right inside the aggregation surface: Krea offers an Ideogram generation entry, while Ideogram's own bench has a fuller feature surface.
It is right inside the aggregation surface: Krea runs Flux in the cloud, Flux weights can be downloaded and run locally.
Also an aggregation relationship: Krea's video line aggregates Veo; see the Veo dossier for the model itself's capability boundaries.
